content.title: Biodiesel
content.description: Biodiesel is a renewable, biodegradable, and eco-friendly fuel produced from vegetable oils, animal fats, or used cooking oils. It can be used directly or blended with diesel in compression ignition (CI) engines.

content.content: Biodiesel is considered an alternative to conventional diesel because it is obtained from renewable biological resources. It burns cleaner, reduces harmful emissions, and helps conserve fossil fuel reserves.

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Biodiesel reduces dependence on petroleum, lowers air pollution, and provides a sustainable fuel for transportation and industrial applications.
Biodiesel is produced from renewable feedstocks such as soybean oil, sunflower oil, palm oil, jatropha oil, mustard oil, animal fats, and waste cooking oils.

Transesterification is the chemical process used to manufacture biodiesel. In this process, vegetable oil or animal fat reacts with an alcohol such as methanol or ethanol in the presence of a catalyst like sodium hydroxide (NaOH) or potassium hydroxide (KOH) to produce biodiesel and glycerol.

content.title: General Reaction
content.code: Triglyceride + Methanol  --(NaOH/KOH)-->  Biodiesel (Fatty Acid Methyl Esters) + Glycerol

content.content: During transesterification, the triglycerides present in vegetable oils react with methanol to form fatty acid methyl esters (biodiesel). Glycerol formed as a by-product settles at the bottom and is separated. The biodiesel is then washed and purified before use.

items.question: Renewable Fuel
items.answer: Produced from plant and animal sources.

items.question: Biodegradable
items.answer: Decomposes naturally without causing long-term pollution.

items.question: High Flash Point
items.answer: Safer to store and transport than conventional diesel.

items.question: Good Lubricity
items.answer: Reduces engine wear and improves lubrication.

items.question: Environment Friendly
items.answer: Produces lower emissions of CO, SO₂, and particulate matter.

items.question: Lower Carbon Emissions
items.answer: Contributes to reduced greenhouse gas emissions.

items.question: Engine Compatibility
items.answer: Can be used in existing diesel engines with little or no modification.

items.question: Biodegradable
items.answer: Less harmful to soil and water in case of spills.

items.question: Transportation
items.answer: Used as fuel in buses, trucks, tractors, and cars.

items.question: Marine Engines
items.answer: Used as an alternative fuel for boats and ships.

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Important questions include the definition of biodiesel, transesterification process with reaction, advantages, and applications.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Biodiesel is a renewable diesel substitute.
Produced from vegetable oils and animal fats.
Methanol and NaOH/KOH are commonly used in production.
Biodiesel reduces pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
Can be used in existing diesel engines.
Widely used in transport, agriculture, and power generation.
